newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat closes lower on Sparks and technicals.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat closes lower on Sparks and technicals.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed lower on a Sparks Companies estimate for 1997 U.S. wheat production at 2.531 billion bushels, above USDA's July outlook for 2.431 billion, traders said.
Also Sparks estimated 1997-98 U.S. wheat ending stocks at 861 million bushels, well above USDA's July forecast for ending stocks at 650 million bushels, traders said.
The market also was hit by follow through technical selling after Monday's drop with news Morocco postponed a tender for 130,000 tonnes of optional origin wheat also cited, the traders said.
But European grain traders Tuesday said Morocco would retender August 12 for 90,000 tonnes of optional soft wheat.
Elevator selling, tied to hedge sales, was noted with FCC a noted seller of one million September. Losses were limited by commercial and mill buying, the traders said.
"There was early buying from Continental then there was some pretty good mill demand," a trader said.
Continental Grain bought two million bushels of September, Benson Quinn and CIS each bought one million September.
KCBT wheat closed one to three cents lower, with September down one at $3.63-1/4.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the KCBT at 28,290 contracts, below the 42,060 traded Monday.
